newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on mild temp forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on mild temp forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Monday in a sluggish session, pressured all day by forecasts this week for milder Northeast and Midwest weather though prices held above key support.
August slipped 3.5 cents to close at $2.068 per million British thermal units. September settled 2.6 cents lower at $2.082. Other deferreds ended down by 1.4 to 2.3 cents.

"People looked at the (mild) weather and didn't think there was enough there to hold it up, so we opened a little softer than expected. But cash is holding a premium to the board and we couldn't break below $2.05," said one trader.

While forecasts this week for milder Northeast and Midwest weather helped trigger some early selling, some traders said futures held fairly steady after the soft open and may be unable to move much lower with cash holding a seven cent premium to paper.
"The cash premium to the board has some people nervous," the Midwest trader said.

While technical traders said August's brief dip Monday below the double bottom at $2.065 was negative, most saw the $2.055 spot continuation low from June 12 as more significant support. Psychological support was seen ahead of $2. Resistance was pegged at $2.11, $2.15 and then along the down trendline at about $2.26. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents to about the $2.10 level. Midcon pipes stayed little changed in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also was quoted a couple of cents higher in the high-$2.30s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip slid 2.1 cents to $2.173. NYMEX said 20,667 contracts traded, little changed from Thursday's revised tally of 20,421.

On the KCBT, August finished 1.7 cents lower at $1.955, while deferreds ended down by 1.2 to 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.8 cents to 11.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 26 lots traded, down from Thursday's total of 91.
